tasks.title: Named limits for transcoding jobs and HLS segments in jellyfin
tasks.initialPrompt: Work on the limits jellyfin uses while it transcodes media and serves HLS segments, inside MediaBrowser.Controller/MediaEncoding, MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding, Jellyfin.Api/Controllers/DynamicHlsController.cs, and MediaBrowser.Model/Dlna/StreamBuilder.cs. The work has five stages; do them in order and finish each before starting the next. Keep evidence.md current throughout, with each requested fact on its own line as `key: value`, a bare integer without digit separators for numeric values, and every such line still present whenever you rewrite the file. Stage 1, read and record. Read MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding/Transcoding/TranscodeManager.cs and MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding/Encoder/MediaEncoder.cs completely, then read Jellyfin.Api/Controllers/DynamicHlsController.cs completely, all in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines. Record these facts about the source as you first read it: `segmented-ping-timeout-ms` (the ping timeout in milliseconds `PingTimer` gives a job that is not progressive), `partial-delete-retry-limit` (the retry count at which `DeletePartialStreamFiles` gives up), `partial-delete-first-delay-ms` (the delay in milliseconds passed to the first attempt at deleting partial stream files after a job is stopped), `sdr-image-timeout-ms` and `hdr-image-timeout-ms` (the default image extraction timeouts in milliseconds for standard and high dynamic range), `segment-gap-numerator` (the number `GetDynamicSegment` divides by the segment length to decide how far a requested segment may be from the current transcoding position), and `muxing-queue-floor` (the smallest muxing queue size `GetCommandLineArguments` passes to the encoder). Stage 2, first edit. In MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding/Transcoding/TranscodeManager.cs, add a private constant named `MaxPartialDeleteRetries` assigned the retry count `DeletePartialStreamFiles` compares against today, and make the comparison use it. Read the changed regions again. Then read the first 4,000 lines of MediaBrowser.Controller/MediaEncoding/EncodingHelper.cs in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines and record `sane-bitrate-ceiling` (the ceiling in bits per second that `EncodingHelper` applies to a video bitrate). Stage 3, second edit. In Jellyfin.Api/Controllers/DynamicHlsController.cs, add a private constant named `SegmentGapSeconds` assigned the number `GetDynamicSegment` divides by the segment length today, and make that division use it. Read the changed regions again. Then read the rest of MediaBrowser.Controller/MediaEncoding/EncodingHelper.cs in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines, and read MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding/Probing/ProbeResultNormalizer.cs completely and record `subtitle-description-length` (the longest subtitle description the probe normalizer extracts). The nine lines recorded so far describe the source before your changes and must keep those values to the end of the session. Stage 4, third edit. In MediaBrowser.Controller/MediaEncoding/EncodingHelper.cs, replace the local constant that holds the video bitrate ceiling with a private class-level constant named `MaxSaneVideoBitrate` that holds the same value, declared directly below the `VulkanAlias` constant, and make the method use it. Read the changed regions again. Then read MediaBrowser.Model/Dlna/StreamBuilder.cs, MediaBrowser.Controller/MediaEncoding/EncodingJobInfo.cs, MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding/Encoder/EncoderValidator.cs, and MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding/Subtitles/SubtitleEncoder.cs completely. Stage 5, three value changes. Change `MaxPartialDeleteRetries` to the value you gave `SegmentGapSeconds` in stage 3. Change `SegmentGapSeconds` to the smallest muxing queue size you recorded. Change `MaxSaneVideoBitrate` to half the value you gave it in stage 4. Use the values as they were before this stage for all three changes. Read the three changed declarations again, then record `partial-delete-retry-limit-after`, `segment-gap-numerator-after`, and `sane-bitrate-ceiling-after` (the values those three constants hold now) in evidence.md. Make no other change to the repository: edit only the three files named, with the edit tool, and do not create, delete, or rename files. Read substantial source ranges, rather than answering from a directory listing or remembered knowledge. After the fifth stage, investigate how the encoder command line differs between a copied and a transcoded video stream for HLS, and which tests under tests/Jellyfin.MediaEncoding.Tests, tests/Jellyfin.MediaEncoding.Hls.Tests and tests/Jellyfin.Model.Tests pin that, until the runner stops live work. tasks.title: One shared step for the cluster rejoin and writable delays in redis
tasks.initialPrompt: Work on the delays and limits redis cluster uses for gossip, failover, state evaluation and slot migration, inside src. The work has five stages; do them in order and finish each before starting the next. Keep evidence.md current throughout, with each requested fact on its own line as `key: value`, a bare integer without digit separators for numeric values, and every such line still present whenever you rewrite the file. Stage 1, read and record. Read src/cluster.h, src/cluster_legacy.h, and src/cluster_asm.h completely, then read src/cluster_legacy.c completely in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines. Record these facts about the source as you first read it: `failover-relog-seconds` (the period in seconds after which the reason a replica cannot fail over is logged again), `rcvbuf-init-bytes` (the initial length in bytes of a cluster link receive buffer), `accepts-per-call` (the largest number of cluster bus connections accepted in one call of the accept handler), `blacklist-ttl-seconds` (the number of seconds a forgotten node stays in the blacklist), `rejoin-delay-max-ms`, `rejoin-delay-min-ms`, and `writable-delay-ms` (the three delays in milliseconds defined directly above `clusterUpdateState`). Stage 2, first edit. Then read src/cluster_asm.c completely in consecutive ranges of about 500 lines and record `asm-aof-min-items` (the minimum number of items per key for which slot migration uses the append-only-file encoding). Change `CLUSTER_REJOIN_DELAY_STEP` to the initial length of a cluster link receive buffer that you recorded. In src/cluster_asm.c, change the minimum number of items per key for the append-only-file encoding to the largest number of cluster bus connections accepted in one call that you recorded.
